If you're someone who has never touched the command line on a *nix system, then this will probably be a game that has a lot more milage for you.  It's a very simplified version of a terminal for a *nix system, and it's not easy to pick up the basic commands it requires you to learn.

On the other hand, if you have ever worked on the command line before, you'll find yourself being pretty frustrated that this game doesn't have a more advanced mode for navigation on the system.  You'll frequently find yourself dumbing down your navigation and wish you had things like:

find
sort
vim/nano -- why can't we manipulate logs in this game?
man (force of habit)
grep

Overall, not a bad game.  Feels a little slow if you have CLI experience, but generally fosters the good general detective work anyone would want to use when tracking something down on a system.

> UPDATED 16 of August. Check below.

An interesting mix between Uplink and Street Hacker, for the price of ~10 USD is definitely worth checking out.

The game is pretty fun, some things require attention to detail and logical thinking, and the humor is pretty good!

However, the game launched with a very bad bug which might make your save useless: if you try to make two missions at a time, you won't be able to complete the first one. This can simply kill your save.
Also, even though the presentation is well done and the interface looks pretty, I don't see much advance over what other Hacking games did before (Uplink was released in 2001), so you really should approach this with caution. The biggest difference here is being able to use both a GUI and a Console - which is good news.

This doesn't detract from the enjoyment of the game, of course. But it does dissapoint if you expected anything more than that.

I haven't finished the game yet, due to the bug that probably broke my savegame. But about the plot: it's decently intriguing and will make you want to uncover all the secrets, as a hacking game should.

So even though I ended up pretty disappointed - it's 2015, yet there's little news here. Even Street Hacker, which is a decade old and terribly programmed, had deeper features; and Uplink had a more compelling gameplay and story - there's still some fun to be had and some jokes/moments actually made me laugh or smile. 
I do recommend waiting for a patch before playing it, though. So rush it on your own risk. :)

Thanks for reading!
-----

UPDATE: As of 16 of August, there has been an update to try and fix some issues. I made a new save and it broke itself again - the game forced me to have two missions at a time, making the first one unable to be complete, which would make it impossible to finish the game.
This release was a REAL mess, and it annoys me that some people are defending the game blindly. After two playthroughs, I was unable to finish it. So please, start taking notes of the facts.

Therefore, I must say that you shouldn't buy this unless you're a fan of the genre - unless all of the gamebreaking and save-corrupting bugs are fixed.

If you are a seasoned gamer then you'll remember a game a lot of reviewers are talking about called UpLink which was a very simular game from eons ago and was a huge cult hit, still is popular to this day. There have been a number of attempts over the years to create a modern day version, but getting the right mix of everything is the hardest part. 

You don't want or need large rendering graphics, but obviously you do need some graphics I mean, just some kind of plain shell console throughout the entire game would really restrict the audience!  HackNet has got that just right in my opinion, there isn't too much, there isn't too little and the graphics that are used in modern developing are not that extensive. 

Such a game has always really been targeted at a specific audience, namely the geeks and nerds and one thing that hasn't changed as much as it's not been completly dumbed down too much terminolgy wise. I mean I know other geeks and nerds and some of those know little about programming, but they can pretty much recite you the episode names for every stark trek series, in order. And HackNet appears to those people too because it has a point and click feature as well as a shell command prompt for those of who us are interesting more in that sense and have had previous exposure to a simular kind of environment over the years. 

You can pretty much come into this game with generally no knowledge about hacking and have an enjoyable experience, and pinking up terminology whilst learning new things along the way. For some of you it could turn out to be a very educational experience. So all in all, I personally think it would be money well spent. Or if you are still cautious, it's worth the risk, you'll know in under two hours or not whether this is the game for you.

The major bug that plagues players right now is that you cannot accept any "jobs" while you have one active. The game will let you do so, but when you do it will render all previously accepted missions impossible to complete. One my first playthrough, I was not aware of this and got hours in before I encountered the bug. Second playthrough I was being careful- only sought out one mission at a time. I look forward to the developer (who is highly active and responisve) fixing these problems and I will update my review to recommend at that time. Until then, I would pass on a purchase but put it on your wishlist for later.

UPDATE- The dev replied to this review directly, which you can see in the comments of this review. That speaks volumes to me that this is a good dev that cares about this game- the kind of dev that I feel that we (the Steam community) need to support. I anticipate changing this review from negative to positive soon.

SECOND UPDATE (07/08/16)- The bugs are now fixed, and this is a really good game highly recommed.

[b]Hacknet[/b] is a hacking simulation game. You are probably familiar with other games of the same genre, such as Uplink and the Hacker Evolution series. This game is, I dare to say, better than both of those, despite having some bugs.
If this review is too long for you, I suggest you to only read the first paragraph about the game's content and the final verdict at the end.

[h1]What is happening in the game:[/h1]
Fourteen days after Agent Bit's disappearance, a failsafe sequence was activated. You are one of the only people who can solve Bit's death. As you get more and more involved into the hacker community, you start unveiling a mystery and it's up to you to discover what was really behind Bit and the security system he created.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[list]
    [*]After the success of Uplink, there had to be a game sooner or later that would try to improve what Uplink started. Hacknet not only achieves that, but takes it to the next level. The story alone is amazing and makes sure that you're not just repeating the same commands and actions over and over but gives it a meaning.
    [*]I have to say that the whole interface is working really nicely when it comes to clarity and effectiveness. You can do 90% of things both in the Display section and Terminal section, but they are both placed in the interface and I find it surprisingly effective. I use the Display section for figuring out what is going on and the Terminal section to execute commands.
    [*]You have a nice map on the bottom of the screen, that is showing all of the cyber locations you have visited already. As you get to connect to tons of computers, you would think that the map would be overcrowded, but this is not the case. I found the map really useful, despite it being almost completely covered.
    [*]There is no bouncing from servers as you remember from other hacking games. Instead, traces are lost if you simply disconnect. Even better is the way how the developers managed what happens if you get traced. Your computer (the virtual one, of course) activates a failsafe sequence. It tells you the IP of your ISP and your IP. You have to break into your ISP's server in a very limited amount of time and from there, reset your IP. This is a brilliant way to prevent accidental game overs and having to start all over again. Instead, you are provided with one more hard (and fun) challenge.
    [*]I really enjoy the soundtrack in this game. The song was written by a guy who also made the soundtrack for Hotline Miami. The music matches with the tension of your current illegal doings and really makes your heart beat faster. Amazing job.
    [*]The in-game hacking is based on actual UNIX commands, which is pretty cool. Still, don't expect to be a pro hacker when you finish this game. You would still be a few steps away, the first step being stopping playing hacking simulators instead of learning the real deal.
    [*]There is a ton of Easter Eggs in this game. A clicker game, hidden Steam keys and a lot more. It's really impressive how they manage to fit all sorts of things into this game. Also, you should read all of the IRC chat logs when you encounter them. They can be super funny (and useful).
    [*]I have cooperated with the developer in bug-related issues and I have to say that I really like the way that the developer interacts with the community. (Almost) all of the bugs I have encountered were fixed and I'm glad that they managed to bring the final release in a shape that they did.
    [*]Another interesting aspect of this game is puzzle solving. You have to think really hard to solve some of them and you even have to remember things from your previous missions, write things down and stuff like that.
    [*]If you don't like the user interface, you will encounter skins later in the game that you can download and make your virtual computer looks just the way you want.
    [*]The system requirements are low, which is great for old computers. However, there are some moments when FPS suddenly drops and gets to a normal level quickly.
    [*]$/€10 is a steal for a game of such quality. If you ever enjoyed hacking games, this should be the top game on your wishlist.
[/list]

[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[list]
    [*]Bugs. Many were fixed, but some are still present. The game-breaking ones are gone, however, so you should be fine.
    [*]This game should have a button to reset progress. I wanted to do that a couple of times but you can't really do that without browsing through folders and files.
[/list]

[h1]The final verdict:[/h1]
As a big fan of hacking games, I was very happy to be able to play Hacknet. The game is certainly made well and definitely recommend this game to you if you enjoy hacking games as well. The story is surprisingly good and adds an important part to the whole experience. The hacking really feels real and, even though that the commands are pretty much the same through the whole game, never feel repetitive.
This is, no doubt, the best hacking game ever released. Get it, and fast!

Greetings,
BirdCute

Sadly, this has to be a [b]not recommended[/b] review.
The reason for this is the apparent lack of quality control before release. See details below.

First off, the concept is great. I really want to love this game for it's concept. It is basically a much better version of Uplink.
Now, is it realistic from a hacking point of view? No. But that's a good thing, because realistic hacking scenarios would be pretty boring for a game. The concepts are taken from the real world and simplified/modified to make an interesting game.

It is simple at first and doesn't get too difficult while still providing some challenges and a nice storyline. 

That being said, while the game could be a 9/10, game-breaking bugs currently make it at most a 4/10.

Here are some that I've encountered so far:
- You are able to take multiple contracts at some point, but doing so will prevent further progression due to the quest completion system being bugged.
- Using multiple profiles is inconsistent, you can't be sure that your savegame remains the way it was
- Game supports windowed mode but crashes regularly if you focus on another window
- Loss of all savegames - this is a big one. The last time the aforementioned crash occured, I've lost all of my saves.

The last bug on this list is the main reason this review has come to a not recommended conclusion and the others severely contributed.
If any beta testing would've been done, such a list of game-breaking bugs wouldn't exist.

Update 1: After the most recent patch promised a solution  to "many issues that were causing people to lose save files" I've decided to start a new profile. Did some work, saved session and exited the game normally. And alas, as I started the game again today there were no accounts and my save_accountsMeta.xml was gone. Again. This is clearly getting ridiculous and I wouldn't expect a solution any time soon, the dev will probably need a few weeks to figure out the issues with Steam API/Cloud saves etc.

Update 2: Since apparently fixing the savegame issues within a reasonable amount of time isn't happening, I have to say this is close to false advertising. The game should be tagged early access if the amount of issues is still that extensive after two patches. This is the sort of behaviour I'd expect from large companies that simply don't give a sh*t anymore, not form an indie dev trying to make his name. I hope the dev learns some things from this failed release, one of them being that you shouldn't release a game full of bugs when you're too busy being at conventions after the release and don't have time to fix the issues.

Don't get me wrong: everyone makes mistakes and stuff like that can happen. But that doesn't change the fact that as a customer I kinda feel cheated, since there's a reason I don't buy early access and this time the product isn't of higher quality.
Again, once the major bugs are fixed and solutions for the existing issues are presented, I'll gladly give this game a recommendation.

There are many secrets to find and it's a fantastic example of attention to detail in game design. A must buy for anyone with a server admin background and those interested in a more realistic approach to hacking in games.

Had an absolute blast with this one. Thoroughly recommended to everyone. The screenshots can look a bit daunting, but the tutorial is comprehensive enough without being insulting. Nice learning curve when you are forced to use the command line only.

Includes a few cool easter eggs, and also a branching path in some areas, making a 2nd play through still enjoyable.

Made by an Australian for an Australian label.
I Absolutely loved everything about this game. So different than anything else I've played in the last years. 10/10 would recommend!

[h1] An updated lite version of Uplink. [/h1]

Hacknet is amazing, but what keeps it from topping Uplink is that it has less features and flexibility. 

[b]Disclaimer: I've not yet completed the entire game. But based on a wild experience I've had with it, I felt prompted to write the review. [/b]

If you played Uplink, this is basically an updated version of the game.  Focused on command consoles, IP, file retrieval/removal all in a neat little interface.

It takes some of the very same queues from Uplink in its story, as you investigate about a hacker named Bit.

Pros:
[list]
[*]Authentic feel
[*]Challenging yet very satisfying
[*]Outstanding music
[/list]

Cons:
[list]
[*]No money system. The fun part of Uplink was going off on the side and robbing banks wirelessly, and using the money to build an unstoppable system, and simply feeling rewarded for your contracts.
[*]No hardware to upgrade. 
[*]Tutorials and in-game info isn't always clear. I know its not supposed to hand-hold. But it feels like many commands are left out, as well as some contracts aren't clear about what they want sometimes. The explanation of Shells and Trapping are complete garbage. That needs to be fixed. 
[*]Lack of freedom. Uplink had a lot more freedom in becoming a white hat, black hat, or grey hat.  Also had more in the way of non-linear gameplay choices. 
[*]Lack of freedom in file editing. In uplink you could change log files, and put someone elses IP in place of your own... Leading to hilarious results as you pin your hacks on someone else. 
[/list]

[b][u]What's awesome:[/u][/b] Unlike Uplink, it gives you a chance at redemption if you fail some missings, and even a chance at revenge. 

[b][u]What's not awesome:[/u][/b] The very linear gameplay.

[b][u]One major letdown [/u][/b]: No sandbox mode/options. 

[b]Overall: Some glaring bad decisions aside, it is a great game. It tense, it makes you feel like a hacker, it has some great polish, and all this for the price its asking is a no brainer. It's a very decent game, but it COULD have been great.  Still waiting for the real Uplink 2 to stand up. [/b]

It's not quite as long as Uplink, but it's better at telling its story. The hacking is a little less varied in some ways, but somehow it feels better despite that. You feel the pressure more, and the basic process for owning a server is a little more involved than most of what you do in Uplink, so it all balances out.

Aside from that: the music is excellent, the UI works well, and the verisimilitude is best in the genre.

I think I actually like it better than Uplink. That's a big statement.

A short, but very sweet, hacking simulator similar to the classic Uplink.  However, Hacknet is much more story-focused and linear, and is closer to being "real" in that you spend a lot of playing time using a UNIX-like command line.  Rock Paper Shotgun called the game more a work of Interactive Fiction than an open hacking sim, and they're pretty much right.

+ Nice use of a faux command-line making you feel l33t instead of just punching "hack" buttons on a UI
+ Straightforward challenges mixed up with a few head scratchers requiring diligent exploration of server contents
+ Great presentation and ease of use
+ Plenty of atmosphere
+ Decent enough story, if a bit predictable once the (few) major players come on the scene
+ Doesn't overstay its welcome with grind

- No real replayability
Fun game, should take a day or a few hours depending on how quick on the uptake you are.

My Review Before Changing To Positive:

I really really want to like this game but for how many times I've had to restart because of a damn game breaker I just can't do it anymore. The game tells you right at the start to make sure and clean your tracks. Well I did this not knowing I was supposed to copy an IP from one of the logs. Can't progress any further. Restart the game.

Oh some dude hacked me and deleted my x-server file, ok, get his IP from my logs, clear my logs, hack him back, steal the x-server file, clear my tracks, reboot, still can't finish the mission. Hack him again, absolutely nothing left on his system. Run out of time, diconnect, reconnect and check for other network connections, nothing, check eos, nothing, disconnect. Can't progress any further yet again. Jesus christ....

One mission even asks you to steal a mailing list and transfer it back to the hiring company. Only it doesn't tell you WHO to transfer it to or HOW to transfer it. The solution was easy, you don't actually have to transfer it to anybody, just delet it. hahaha, seriously, this game....

I've only got 3 hours logged and I had to check the forums on WTF i'm supposed to do or how i'm supposed to progress probably 3 times. That's pretty poor.

You want to play a really good hacking game? Play Uplink. This game is a mess.


Why I Changed My Review To Positive:

I do have fun while i'm playing it, that I can't deny. It sucks that one small mistake can halt the progression of the game causing you to have to restart, and it glitches and breaks sometimes, but once you KNOW about these downfalls, you then know what to look out for while playing. It grew on me I guess.

Hacknet is a game where player takes the role of a hacker in search of the mysterious story of Bit, another hacker.
The game requires the use of the terminal, but GUI is available too for convenience. 
For those that came looking for an experience similar to Uplink, I would say for the experience you get in Uplink, Hacknet definitely nailed it. Differences being that Hacknet is more terminal oriented and is more story oriented.
Instead of comparing the game to Uplink, Hacknet can be compared to "Digital: A Love Story", which is also a hacker, story driven game.

Another strong point of Hacknet is the story. The story drives the entire game. It starts slowly, but gets progressively more and more tense, starting to put your abilities to the limit, especially at the end *wink wink*

Do I recommend it? Of course.
A masterpiece!

As a lifelong computer geek nerd I have always sucked at coding and command line stuff. Back in school I was bad at languages and good at science, maths and creative stuff so I blame my sucky coding skills on this. 

I have however always been a fan of hacking games such as the Uplink and Hacker Evolution series but they have always felt more like hacking from the movie hackers rather than what actual hacking might be like. Hacknet is much closer to what I imagine it is like and I really enjoyed the time I spent with it. The game was easy to get into and moves at a decent pace with an intuitive difficulty curve that meant I never felt I knew exactly what to do but equally never floundered and got stuck.  

As far as I understand this isn’t really an accurate sim of any kind of software it is instead an adventure game with a DOS style command line interface. There are some graphical elements to help things along but the game, at least to an outsider, feels very real.

There were a few times that I got stuck but this was nothing that a few moments checking the help page did not fix. If anything one of the things I feel could have really benefitted this game would be multi-monitor support. It was really annoying to have to flick between windows as opposed to having multiple windows open at the same time. 

The game is relatively difficult but not unfair but I think someone with a better knowledge of command line interfaces might have found it easier.

As you progress through the game you begin to understand more about the world you live in as the story evolves in front of you. There are a fair amount of pop culture references that always raise a smile. 

Overall Hack Net is well worth playing to anyone who watched hackers or Jurassic Park and wanted to feel like they were shit hot at computering.

Finally a new Uplink-style hacking puzzler! Enjoyable, but a bit on the simple side. The visuals are pleasing, all the hacking tools look nice when they run. The music tracks are great.

The game is not as long as I would've hoped for. According to steam 8 hours but that figure is somewhat inflated. Probably offers a good 7 hours of gameplay.

During my playthrough I know I missed how to stop a hacker in time, so maybe I'll replay at some point. Don't know if I missed anything else. I feel the replay value is probably quite low, as the missions seem to be pretty much static.

However, if there ever was a sequel/dlc/addon for this game I would definately buy it. Hopefully with more hacking tools and a ton of new missions. More complexity please!

I'd hoped for maybe some sort of mini-games when you run some of these hacking tools, but essentially they all work the same way. Run the tool and wait. (so, maybe more things to do like how analyzing firewalls works?) Also I think the end-game was disappointing, story, and lengthwise, and not being able to use those things you saw on entech servers. I just wish there was more depth to it, more things to do and to explore, more tools, more story, more missions, more everything..

Also the game is clearly not designed for 2560x1600, ended up playing at half-res, The game did crash a few times, but I was able to recover from a nearby auto-save each time so it was okay. Probably those few bugs will be fixed soon.


Overall;

[b]6.5/10[/b]
